rule: Elixir: `Module.fun`; ... remote calls `Mod.fun` medium unless defined in the scan | `:erlang_mod.f` and an imported Erlang module are `erlang_mod.f`. | Anonymous functions, lambdas ... fold into the nearest enclosing named function | Not calls: passing a method reference
notes: call_type convention (SPEC gives no Elixir mapping; Elixir has no methods and the `macro` type is defined only for C/C++/ObjC and Rust `name!`): every local, imported and remote call is direct, a call through a value is callback. Operators and special forms (`|>`, `=`, `case`, `fn`, `%{}`, `__MODULE__`) are language constructs, not calls. Bare Kernel functions resolve to the auto-imported Kernel (Elixir decision: 'with one import known to export the name, that import is the target'): `Kernel.<name>`, medium. `clean(w)` is inside an anonymous `fn` passed to Enum.map, so it folds into `MyApp.Text.normalize`; it is a local call to a defp of the module (high). `&blank?/1` is a function capture (a reference), not a call. The two `blank?` clauses are declarations. Each pipe stage is on its own line.
